Durations: Temporal's Duration

Source: R/duration.R
duration.Rd

A duration() is a length of time in ten fields, years to nanoseconds, each a float64-representable integer as Temporal defines them, stored as a list of ten double vectors (design 4.1). All fields share one sign. Years, months and weeks are calendar units: operations that need their length take relative_to, a date, and fail without it (design 6.5).

Usage

duration(
  years = 0,
  months = 0,
  weeks = 0,
  days = 0,
  hours = 0,
  minutes = 0,
  seconds = 0,
  milliseconds = 0,
  microseconds = 0,
  nanoseconds = 0,
  ...
)

duration_compare(x, y, relative_to = NULL)

Arguments

years

The years, or a string in ISO 8601 form ("P1Y2M3DT4H5M6.789S", a fraction only on the smallest unit present), or a duration() to return as is.

months, weeks, days, hours, minutes, seconds, milliseconds, microseconds, nanoseconds

The remaining fields, 0 by default.

...

Must be empty.

x, y

duration() values or strings, for duration_compare().

relative_to

A plain_date(), plain_date_time() or a string either reads: the date the calendar units are counted from. Required when either duration has years, months or weeks.

Value

A duration() vector; duration_compare() returns an integer vector of -1, 0 and 1.

Examples

duration("P1Y2M3DT4H5M6.789S")
#> <zutempo_duration[1]>
#> [1] P1Y2M3DT4H5M6.789S
duration(hours = 25)
#> <zutempo_duration[1]>
#> [1] PT25H
duration(milliseconds = 2^53 + 2)
#> <zutempo_duration[1]>
#> [1] PT9007199254740.994S
duration_compare("PT1H", "PT60M")
#> [1] 0
duration_compare("P1M", "P30D", relative_to = "2026-02-01")
#> [1] -1
